title: Electric Charge: Like Charges Repel, Unlike Attract
subject: Physics
objective: Those sparks when you pull off a sweater come from electric charge. How rubbing moves electrons, what positive and negative mean, and why like charges repel.

fill.q: Rubbing transfers ____ from one body to another.
A body that loses electrons becomes ____.
A body that gains electrons becomes ____.

tf.q: Glass rubbed with silk becomes positive.
tf.explain: It loses electrons to the silk.

tf.q: Plastic rubbed with fur becomes negative.
The total charge of a rubbed pair is zero if both began neutral.

ar.a: The total charge of a neutral pair stays zero after rubbing.
ar.r: Electrons only move from one body to the other.

ar.a: A rubbed glass rod repels another rubbed glass rod.
ar.r: Both carry the same kind of charge.

mcq.q: A positive and a negative object will:
Sparks from a sweater come from:

num.q: A neutral rod gives 5 electrons to a cloth. What is the rod's charge, in units of e?
After rubbing, a body has +6 units of charge. What is its neutral partner's charge now?

short.q: Why does a sweater spark when pulled off?
short.solution: Rubbing moves electrons so opposite charges build up on the sweater and shirt; they discharge as a spark.

match.explain: Each rubbed object matches its charge.
